expressiveness_gaps: SKILL_CF_BEASTMASTER_PACK_TACTICS (the pet half of Pack Tactics) is authored per the coverage matrix's sketch but has no pack-owned pet Character config to attach it to in CF_PACK_EOR_CLASSES — pets/mercs are Summoner's domain (matrix §5 note 7). The recipe is valid and PackCheck-clean but currently unreachable in-game until a pet config references it in its own Passives[].

SKILL_CF_PRIEST_BENEDICTION: the coverage matrix's sketch (§1 row 20) gates PRIEST's _01-tier status pair on ROLL_TIER(EQ PERFECT) under ON_HEAL, closing BM's 'tiered status choice by roll grade' gap via per-effect Conditions. The shipped ClassForge.Recipes engine's HealEvent (Runtime/TriggerEvents.cs) does not carry a roll-tier field for ON_HEAL (only Healer/Healed/AbilityId/Amount) — RecipeValidator confirms this with a W_NO_ROLL_DATA finding ('ON_HEAL carries no pRollData; ROLL_TIER reads the default tier'). A ROLL_TIER condition there would always read the RollTier.SUCCESS default, so it can never distinguish PERFECT and would silently always resolve to the non-perfect branch. Rather than ship a recipe whose Conditions look meaningful but are dead code, this pack authors PRIEST as always-_00 (the honestly-expressible subset) and records the tier split as unported pending an engine change that threads pRollData through ON_HEAL.

GAMBLER's loss chance changes from EOR's chained 7.5% to v1.1's independent-rolls 10% (deliberate, SPEC-DELTA §5.1 ProcChance semantics)
